item.title: Australia news live: Wong speaks to Palestinian foreign minister about Gaza; Queensland premier says plans to reduce visas are ‘nuts’
item.description:
Follow the day’s news live

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Dan Tehan says fuel excise cut when oil price high a ‘sensible’ plan

Dan Tehan, the shadow minister for energy, said Gallagher’s criticism of the Coalition’s fuel plan wasn’t fair.

[What] I would say to Anthony Albanese and the Labor party is get out amongst the people and see what’s happening in your electorates because people are hurting because of cost of living …

We have the discipline to be able to do the policy work to make sure we can offset policies like this so it won’t be inflationary and it will provide much needed relief to people, and they need it now.

Obviously we’ve helped when the war started with some changes to the fuel excise but we’ve shifted, and [are] including in the budget, to providing more permanent cost of living arrangements, including through the tax system, to make sure that that ongoing cost-of-living help is there permanently, not just in these one-off arrangements, which, when we’ve got higher inflation, could be difficult in the economy.

Our decisions have been built and baked into the budget to make sure that that cost-of-living help is permanent. You know, the sooner this war in the Middle East stops, the better.

item.title: Ukraine targets Moscow with hundreds of drones on final day of Russian election
item.description:
At least three people killed and oil refinery damaged as doubts cast over initial reports of ballistic missile use

Ukraine has targeted Moscow and the surrounding region in a large-scale attack that involved hundreds of drones.

The attack killed at least three people and damaged what Ukraine’s president, Volodymyr Zelenskyy, said was one of Russia’s “key oil industry facilities” on the final day of the country’s parliamentary elections, authorities said on Sunday.

Continue reading...

item.title: Middle East braces for more violence as Iran claims US is planning to renew bombing campaign
item.description:
Tensions grow as Trump tells Fox News he is considering ‘wiping Iran out’ after attacks on Riyadh by Houthi rebels

Governments across the Middle East are bracing for an escalation of violence after Iran claimed it had received intelligence that the US was preparing for a renewed bombing campaign against the Islamic Republic.

In a potential sign of growing tensions before the UN general assembly in New York this week, Donald Trump cut short a weekend visit to the Camp David presidential retreat on Sunday with no official explanation, and a new security alert was issued by the state department to all US citizens in the Middle East.

item.title: Thick smoke seen near Riyadh airport as Houthis claim attack on Saudi capital
item.description:
Authorities issued warnings for city in first such alerts for Riyadh since fighting with Iran-backed Houthis escalated in July

Yemen’s Houthis said they attacked “sensitive” sites in the Saudi capital with missiles and drones, hours after flames and a large plume of black smoke were seen rising above Riyadh airport on Saturday.

The Saudi government sent air raid alerts to citizens by phone overnight warning of aerial attacks, marking the first time the government has issued such alerts for Riyadh since fighting with the Iran-backed Houthis escalated in July.

Continue reading...

item.title: Yemen’s anti-Houthi forces launch inquest into sudden military collapse
item.description:
Rout raises questions about coordination and morale as some politicians claim billions of dollars were offered to persuade forces to abandon position

A bitter inquest is under way among Yemen’s anti-Houthi forces as to how what was being billed as a decisive assault on Sana’a, the Houthi-controlled capital, suddenly collapsed into a military rout.

More than 15 brigades were defeated as the country’s entire west coast fell into Houthi hands. Efforts are now being made to reorganise the anti-Houthi forces representing the UN-recognised Yemeni government in order to capture the Kahbob mountains, a strategic point from which to restrict Houthi forces moving closer to the crucial Bab al-Mandab strait.

Continue reading...

item.title: Houthis claim drone attack on Saudi Arabia's capital after smoke seen rising near airport
item.description: Yemen's Iran-backed Houthis have claimed responsibility for missile and drone attacks targeting "sensitive" sites in Saudi Arabian capital Riyadh - hours after flames and smoke were seen near the city's main airport.

item.title: Yemen's Giants Brigades claim attacks on Houthi military vehicles, say all aboard killed
item.description:
Yemen's Giants Brigades claim attacks on Houthi military vehicles, say all aboard killed

Yemen’s government-affiliated Giants Brigades claimed attacks on five Houthi military vehicles on the Kahbub front overlooking the strategic Bab al-Mandab Strait, killing everyone aboard.

item.title: Four civilians killed in Yemen's Al-Jawf
item.description:
Four civilians killed in Yemen's Al-Jawf

Air strikes targeting telecommunications towers Yemen's Al-Jawf governorate killed four civilians and injured three others on Sunday, the Houthi-run Yemen News Agency (SABA) reported.

According to a local source speaking to SABA, the casualties were workers.

item.title: A dozen vessels transit Hormuz Strait over the weekend
item.description:
A dozen vessels transit Hormuz Strait over the weekend

A total of 12 vessels transited the Strait of Hormuz on Saturday and Sunday, shipping date showed on Monday. 

The figure is down from 35 during the previous weekend.
